reasoning: HPL 2.3 (xhpl) is a real HPC benchmark — CPU-only build (accelerator none, no gpu_libs), so needs_gpu=false and no GPU vendor requirement. Among the amd64 variants (latest, c2d, c4, vtune, libfabric) all are the same GCC 11.4 / OpenBLAS / OpenMPI xhpl build; the :libfabric tag is the best choice for a 4-node MPI run because its OpenMPI ships mca_mtl_ofi.so linked against libfabric.so.1 which in turn links libefa.so.1, giving it a genuine high-speed OFI/EFA path while still falling back to TCP. The :vtune tag adds only profiling overhead and c2d/c4 are cloud-instance-specific tunings with no fabric support. Network lists efa first (preferred, matches the libfabric/EFA build) and ethernet as an acceptable fallback since OpenMPI's TCP BTL works everywhere. Command is simply the xhpl binary, which reads HPL.dat from the working directory; no mpirun prefix since the runtime launches ranks, and no core/rank counts since nodes are exclusive and the transform derives the process grid P*Q from the matched cluster. Memory: HPL is deliberately sized to fill most of available RAM (the matrix is N^2 doubles), and a well-sized 4-node run on modern nodes uses tens of GB per node, so 64-192GB is the right range — a 0-16GB node would force an uselessly tiny N or OOM during panel factorization. Duration 1800s covers a meaningful problem size at this scale.
